A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Puzzle and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained experiments can be matched across renumbering, including v1 Table 14 and v4 Table 15. Apparent cell errors in v4 Table 16 limit interpretation of individual entries but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model accuracy and throughput measurements, architectural ablations, a blind human evaluation, and RULER results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds Nemotron-49B-Base long-context and before/after-alignment results in Section 7 and Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The block library, initialization, BLD, MIP search, and GKD objectives remain unchanged. Section 7 adds an optional RLHF and instruction-tuning stage for Nemotron-49B-Base, extending the training procedure without revising the core Puzzle algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 adds Arena Hard evaluation and substantially expands long-context task coverage with single-needle, multi-needle, multi-value, and multi-query retrieval tasks in Table 16. Both versions already evaluate contexts through 128K; the original RULER subset and results remain in v4 Table 15.

E2.justification: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct becomes an additional evaluated parent comparator in the new Nemotron-49B-Base comparisons. The existing Llama-3.1, Llama-3.2-3B, Mixtral, and alternative-search comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v4 adds substantial new training and evaluation protocols: a Llama-3.3-derived 49B model receives an additional 5B tokens at 64K context and 5B at 128K, followed by a separate 25M-token alignment experiment. v1's Nemotron-51B training used sequences only through 8K. These are additional experiments; the original hardware and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Table 5 tests alignment compatibility through a direct comparison of Nemotron-49B-Base before and after alignment. The long-context analysis also extends to the newly uptrained model, although it does not isolate long-context uptraining through a same-model ablation. The extensive original Section 8 analyses remain.

E5.justification: The human study still uses 169 samples, three annotators per sample, and randomized completion order; HumanEval still reports n=20. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised. The removed nonsignificance assertion changes a reported conclusion rather than a documented statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial RULER and alignment results. Table 4 reports child/parent averages of 87.39/88.91 at 64K and 49.62/52.25 at 128K under the new model and training conditions. Table 5 reports alignment changes of 8.77 to 9.21 on MT-Bench, 65.8 to 82.1 on Arena Hard, and 81.03 to 80.98 on MMLU. The matched decoupled-BLD accuracy changes from 72.92 to 73.10 in v1 Table 6 versus v4 Table 7. Original Nemotron-51B results remain; the human-evaluation nonsignificance claim is withdrawn without changing the plotted percentages.

T1.justification: The channel-contribution derivation, BLD loss, MIP formulation and diversity constraint, and GKD loss equations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract adds claims that Puzzle can preserve long-context capabilities and produce derivatives that surpass their parent on selected benchmarks after lightweight alignment. It also narrows the 98.4% preservation statement from general capabilities to benchmark accuracies. The main NAS, efficiency, and low-training-cost contributions remain.

C2.justification: v1 proposes longer-context fine-tuning as a possible remedy; v4 presents the new model as demonstrating that remedy and interprets the alignment experiment as evidence of continued adaptability. This extension uses a different parent and RULER subset. The human-evaluation interpretation is softened from statistical nonsignificance to comparable performance.

D1.justification: v4 documents the new long-context training lengths and token budgets, the 25M-token alignment budget, and the referenced alignment recipe. It also adds a model-release link for Llama-3.3-Nemotron-Super-49B. Implementation disclosures for the original Puzzle experiments are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Gromov et al. on deeper-layer redundancy, Li et al. on Arena Hard, and Wang et al. on HelpSteer2-Preference. Its positioning relative to decomposed NAS methods such as DNA, DONNA, and LANA remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and long-context discussion are rewritten, Section 7 gains an alignment paragraph, and Appendix B is divided into model-specific subsections. There are also local wording, author-list, and acknowledgment edits. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 receives larger, rearranged labels while retaining its percentages. The main RULER summary is replaced with the new model comparison, alignment Table 5 and appendix Table 16 are added, and existing tables are locally relocated or renumbered. Table 16 is densely scaled and contains apparent duplicated or misaligned cells; the other figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens practical validation with a directly comparable before/after-alignment experiment and an implemented long-context extension where v1 offered a hypothesis. The gain is limited because the long-context comparison changes both parent model and task subset, and Table 16 contains apparent column errors that weaken verification of some detailed results. The core method and its original empirical support remain intact.
